title: EEOC settles first AI hiring discrimination lawsuit against iTutorGroup for automatic age-based rejection
description: The US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission sued iTutorGroup (and affiliated entities), alleging its job-application software was programmed to automatically reject female applicants aged 55+ and male applicants aged 60+, resulting in over 200 US-based tutoring applicants being rejected because of their age. In August 2023 iTutorGroup agreed to pay $365,000 to the affected applicant class and to adopt anti-discrimination policies, training, monitoring, and a ban on collecting applicant birthdates during initial screening; a federal court approved the consent decree the following month. It is described by the EEOC as the agency's first settlement of an AI-related employment discrimination lawsuit.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty. Underlying rejections reportedly occurred March-April 2020; EEOC lawsuit filed May 2022; this record uses the EEOC's public settlement announcement date.

root_cause: Hiring software was configured with hard-coded age-and-gender cutoff rules that automatically rejected applicants above certain ages, operating as a categorical, automated proxy for age discrimination at the initial applicant-screening stage.

citations.title: iTutorGroup to Pay $365,000 to Settle EEOC Discriminatory Hiring Suit

relationships.reason: A pre-deployment bias audit requirement would have surfaced this categorical age-based auto-rejection logic before it screened any real applicants.
This settlement is a concrete example of the regulatory exposure this board question is designed to pre-empt.
